hint: Match the pieces of a right Riemann sum: the width $\Delta x = \frac{b - a}{n}$ and the sample point $x_k = a + k\Delta x$.

hints.text: Match the pieces of a right Riemann sum: the width $\Delta x = \frac{b - a}{n}$ and the sample point $x_k = a + k\Delta x$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $\sum \frac{1}{n}\left(\frac{k}{n}\right)^2$ has $\Delta x = \frac{1}{n}$ and $x_k = 0 + \frac{k}{n}$, so $a = 0$, $b = 1$, and it becomes $\int_0^1 x^2 \, dx$.
Here $\Delta x = \frac{3}{n}$, so $b - a = 3$. And $x_k = 2 + \frac{3k}{n}$ means $a = 2$. The function applied to $x_k$ is squaring.
With $a = 2$, $b = 5$ and $f(x) = x^2$, the limit is $\int_2^5 x^2 \, dx$, which is choice A.

explanation: A right Riemann sum has the form $\sum_{k=1}^{n} f(a + k\Delta x) \, \Delta x$ with $\Delta x = \frac{b - a}{n}$.
Here $\Delta x = \frac{3}{n}$ (so the interval has length $3$) and $a + k\Delta x = 2 + \frac{3k}{n}$ (so $a = 2$ and $b = 5$). The summand squares $x_k$, so $f(x) = x^2$.
The limit is $\int_2^5 x^2 \, dx = \frac{125 - 8}{3} = 39$. Choice A. (Choice C uses the right interval but squares $2 + x$ again, double-counting the shift.)

alternativeExplanations.title: A second correct reading
steps: You could also read $\frac{3k}{n}$ as $x_k$ on $[0, 3]$ and the summand as $f(x_k) = (2 + x_k)^2$: that gives $\int_0^3 (2 + x)^2 \, dx$.
That integral also equals $39$ — it is the same area shifted left by $2$. Both readings are valid; only A appears among the choices.
Choice B drops the shift entirely and gives $\int_0^3 x^2 = 9$, a different number.
